a: ‘Glorifying Allah’: sanctifying Him and declaring Him free of everything that does not befit Him, and obeying Him.

Musa is a messenger whom Allah the Exalted sent to Pharaoh and his people, and supported with two miracles: one of them is the staff that swallowed the serpents; the other was his hand, which he would put into his bosom and it would come out white without any blemish. Musa called to the oneness of Allah, so Pharaoh fought him and gathered the sorcerers against him to plot against him, but he defeated them by the permission of Allah the Exalted. Then Allah commanded him to leave Egypt with those who followed him, and Pharaoh pursued him with a great army; and when his followers thought they would be overtaken, Allah commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, so that it would be his salvation and the destruction of Pharaoh, whom Allah made a lesson for others.
Qawm: a group of men and women.
‘Ya’ is for calling; ‘qawmi’: my group of men and women.
‘Why do you hurt me’: why do you inflict harm upon me.
‘Inna’: a particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.

The messenger among the angels is the one who conveys the divine message from Allah; the messenger among people is the one whom Allah sends with a law, to act upon it and convey it; the messenger here is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

‘Isa: he is ‘Isa son of Maryam, the messenger of Allah and His word which He cast to Maryam; Allah created him from dust just as He created Adam, and said to him: “Be!” and he was; and he is the one who gave glad tidings of the Prophet Muhammad; Allah gave him the clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit, and he was distinguished in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near; he spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity, and he would create from clay the likeness of a bird, breathe into it, and it would become a bird, and heal the blind-born and the leper, and bring forth the dead — all by Allah’s permission; the Messiah called his people to worship Allah, the One, the Unique, but they refused, were arrogant and opposed him, and none believed in him except the simple folk of his people; Allah raised him to heaven, and he will descend, when Allah wills, to the earth to be a witness over people.
‘Son of Maryam’: he was named after his mother because he has no father.

The daughter of ‘Imran, whom her mother vowed to worship while she was in her womb; the nobles of the Children of Israel competed for her guardianship, and Zakariyya, the husband of her maternal aunt, became her guardian; whenever he entered upon her in the prayer-niche, he found provision with her and would ask her: “From where is this for you?” and she would say: “It is from Allah”; and she is Maryam the Chaste, the mother of ‘Isa, peace be upon him.
The Children of Israel: those who trace their lineage to Israel; and they were twelve tribes.

He is the Prophet Ya‘qub son of Ishaq; ‘Israel’ means ‘servant of Allah’; he was a prophet to his people and he was God-fearing; the angels gave glad tidings of him to his grandfather Ibrahim and his wife Sarah, peace be upon them both; and he is the father of Yusuf, peace be upon him.
‘Inna’: a particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
The messenger: the bearer of the divine message, whether he is a human prophet or an angel among the angels; and the messenger here is ‘Isa, peace be upon him.

The Book of Allah sent down upon Musa, peace be upon him.
‘Giving glad tidings of a messenger’: informing of him and bearing witness to his truthfulness.

‘Ba‘d’: a vague adverb whose meaning is understood by annexation to what follows it; it is the opposite of ‘before’.
